dedupe_keys.name: asiaq technical base map of greenland towns and settlements buildings roads utilities ports and airports free download by locality

description: The technical base map (teknisk grundkort) produced by Asiaq Greenland Survey is the detailed large-scale map of Greenland's towns and settlements. Contents: a technical topographic vector map with roads and paths, buildings with building numbers and house numbers, building use, technical installations and utilities, ports and airports, streams, lakes, land use and place names, plus a digital terrain model and contour lines, orthophotos and cartographic raster maps at 1:2,750 and 1:5,000, and a generalised G50 version. Producer: Asiaq, from aerial and drone photogrammetry and RTK GNSS field survey. Coverage: 74 localities on the map service file server, from Nanortalik in the south to Qaanaaq, each with its own folder; the Nuuk shapefile package was 86 MB and dated 28 September 2026. Format and access: free download since January 2018 from the Asiaq map service as DWG, file geodatabase, shapefile, PDF and orthophoto folders per locality, with a web map display on the NunaGIS portal. Free under Asiaq's terms of use for geodata; historical data are not included. Caveats: coverage is limited to built-up areas, so there is no national road or grid network between towns, and layer names follow Danish and Greenlandic conventions. Asiaq also keeps a 3D sewer map for 15 towns (wells, mains, outlets with material, dimension and year), which is supplied on request, not downloaded. Simulation uses: building and utility exposure for coastal flooding, permafrost thaw and landslide studies in Arctic settlements, and base geometry for town-level infrastructure models. Related records: Statistics Greenland tables on Nukissiorfiit electricity, heat and water sales by town (data-statistics-greenland-statbank-nukissiorfiit-electricity-heat-water-sales-by-town-and-dwelling-stock).
